outputs.exact_statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ be a homogeneous regular sequence in $\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$. There exist a finitely generated field extension $k/\mathbb C$, a finite-dimensional central division $k$-algebra $\Delta$, and a commutative graded $k$-subalgebra $$k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subseteq A\subseteq\Delta[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$$ generated by finitely many pairwise commuting linear forms, with distinguished $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in A_1$, such that $$\label{eq:construction-triangular}
 t_i^{a_i}=c_i f_i+\sum_{l<i}B_{il}f_l+\sum_{d>i}C_{id}t_d
 \qquad(1\le i\le n).$$ Here $c_i\in k^\times$, $B_{il}\in A_{a_i-a_l}$, and $C_{id}\in A_{a_i-1}$. Moreover, $A$ is finite over $k[x]$, and $$\{t_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots t_n^{\alpha_n}:
             \alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n\}$$ is a basis of the full polynomial algebra $\Delta[x]$ as a left $\Delta$-vector space.

Let $n\ge1$ and $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$. Suppose that a homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ contains a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$. There is a monomial ideal $J\subseteq\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ such that $$x_i^{a_i}\in J\quad(1\le i\le n),
 \qquad
 H_{S/J}(d)=H_{S/I}(d)\quad\text{for every }d\ge0.$$

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $S_F=F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be standard graded, and let $$1\le c\le n,\qquad 2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c.$$ If a homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq S_F$ contains a homogeneous regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $\deg f_i=a_i$, there is a monomial ideal $J\subseteq S_F$ containing $P_F=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c})$ such that $$\dim_F(S_F/J)_d=\dim_F(S_F/I)_d\qquad(d\ge0).$$ Moreover, $J$ may be chosen lex-plus-powers: in each degree its monomials outside $P_F$ are the lexicographically greatest $\dim_F I_d-\dim_F(P_F)_d$ monomials outside $P_F$, for the order $x_1>\cdots>x_n$.

Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$, $k$, $\Delta$, $A$, and $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma 4. For every homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq S=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ containing the $f_i$, there is one monomial ideal $J\subseteq S$ such that $$x_i^{a_i}\in J\quad(1\le i\le n),\qquad \dim_\mathbb C(S/J)_d=\dim_\mathbb C(S/I)_d\quad(d\ge0).$$
The space $\mathfrak j_b$ is base-point-free on $\mathbb P(U^\vee)$.

Let $U$ be a vector space of dimension at least three over a characteristic-zero field, and let $b\ge2$. Suppose that $Q\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}U$ is generated in degrees one and two, and that its geometric characteristic set contains no integral curve of degree at most $b(b-1)$. Let $\mathfrak j_b\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^b U$ be a base-point-free subspace containing $(Q)_b$, and define $W$ by [eq:stage-annihilator]. Then every nonzero element of $W$, after any algebraically closed extension, has an irreducible factor of multiplicity one.

For integers $n\ge2$ and $D\ge1$, there is an integer $d_*(n,D)$ with the following property. If $\Omega$ is an algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb C$ and $Z\subseteq\mathbb P^{n-1}_\Omega$ is an integral curve of degree at most $D$, then $Z$ is defined over an algebraically closed intermediate field $F_0\subseteq\Omega$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_\mathbb CF_0\le d_*(n,D)$.

For every $n\ge1$ and $D\ge1$, there exist data $k,\Delta_0,U,Q$ satisfying conditions (i)–(iii) above and the condition on $\mathcal C(Q)$. They may be chosen with $$U=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n,s_1,\ldots,s_m\rangle_k, \qquad Q=(s_\rho^2-q_\rho(x):1\le\rho\le m),$$ where $m\ge2$ and the coefficient vectors of the quadrics $q_\rho$ are jointly algebraically independent over $\mathbb C$.

Let $U\subseteq\widetilde U$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, and let $Q\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}U$ and $\widetilde Q\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}\widetilde U$ be homogeneous ideals, with $Q\subseteq\widetilde Q$. Suppose that $\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}\widetilde U/\widetilde Q$ is finite over $\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}U/Q$. Then the induced projection of characteristic sets is everywhere defined and finite, and pulls back $\mathcal O(1)$ to $\mathcal O(1)$. In particular, if the first characteristic set contains no integral curve of degree at most $D$ after algebraically closed extension, neither does the second.

Let $w$ be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $b\ge2$ on a complex vector space $U$. Suppose that some irreducible factor of $w$ has multiplicity one. Then $w^{-1}(1)$ is connected. For every $M\ge1$, the smooth hypersurface $$F_w=\left\{(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_M)\in U^{\oplus M}:
                 \sum_{m=1}^M w(\ell_m)=1\right\}$$ has the homotopy type of the join of $M$ copies of $w^{-1}(1)$. Consequently, $$\widetilde H_j(F_w;\mathbb Z)=0\qquad(0\le j\le2M-2).$$

Let $k$ be a field admitting an embedding into $\mathbb C$, let $U$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space with $\dim U\ge3$, and let $$W\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^b(U^\vee),\qquad b\ge2,\qquad s=\dim W.$$ Assume that every nonzero element of $W_{\bar k}$ has an irreducible factor of multiplicity one over an algebraic closure $\bar k$. For integers $h\ge2$ and $M\ge2h+4s+10$, put $N_*=M\dim U$ and define $$\begin{split}
 Y&=\left\{(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_M)\in U^{\oplus M}:
                 \sum_{m=1}^M w(\ell_m)=0\quad(w\in W)\right\},\\
 X&=\mathbb P(Y)\subseteq\mathbb P(U^{\oplus M}).
 \end{split}$$ Then $X$ is a geometrically integral complete intersection of codimension $s$, cut out by $s$ equations of degree $b$, and $$\operatorname{codim}_X\operatorname{Sing}X
       \ge M-2s+1>h,$$ with the codimension of the empty locus understood to be infinite. In particular, a general $h$-dimensional projective linear section is a smooth complete intersection contained in [(eq:parameter-jacobian)](#eq:parameter-jacobian)$X_{\mathrm{sm}}$.*

*After any embedding $k\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, let $Y^o$ be the nonzero cone over $X_{\mathrm{sm}}$. Both $Y^o$ and its unit-norm retract are $(M+2h)$-connected.

Let $b\ge2$, fix a primitive $b$-th root $\zeta$, and put $$G=(\mu_b^b/\mu_b)\rtimes(\mathbb Z/b),\qquad e=b^b,$$ where the denominator is the diagonal subgroup and $\mathbb Z/b$ permutes the $b$ factors cyclically. There are smooth connected projective curves $C,T_0$, a connected étale $G$-cover $C\to T_0$, and a genuinely $G$-linearized line bundle $L$ on $C$ with the following properties.*

1.  *The genera and degree satisfy $$g_T:=g(T_0)=b-1,\qquad g(C)-1=e(g_T-1),\qquad \deg L=e.$$*


2.  *There are sections $a_\alpha\in H^0(C,L)$, indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^b$ with $|\alpha|=b$, whose transport follows the degree-$b$ monomial representation in formal homogeneous coordinates $p_0,\ldots,p_{b-1}$. The notation $p^\alpha$ labels the section $a_\alpha$ when $|\alpha|=b$; it does not assign individual sections of $L$ to the $p_j$. Write $a_\alpha=p^\alpha$ and set $$z=\frac1b\sum_{j=0}^{b-1}p_j^b,\qquad
     u=-\frac1b\sum_{j=0}^{b-1}\zeta^{-j}p_j^b,\qquad
     v=p_0\cdots p_{b-1}.$$ They satisfy $$\label{eq:binary-section-relations}
     p_j^b=z-\zeta^ju,\qquad z^b=u^b+v^b.$$ The section $z$ is invariant, and $u,v$ have characters $\chi,\psi:G\to\mu_b$, respectively. The pencil $u,v$ is base-point-free and defines a degree-$e$ morphism $\pi:C\to\mathbb P^1$ with $L=\pi^*\mathcal O(1)$.*



3.  *For a generic $A\in\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^0(C)$, over its field of definition $\kappa$, the space $E_A=H^0(C,A L^{g_T})$ has dimension $e$. Multiplication of sections gives isomorphisms $$\label{eq:curve-free-module}
     H^0(C,A L^{g_T+j})
       =E_A\otimes_\kappa\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^j_\kappa\langle u,v\rangle
           \qquad(j\ge0).$$ Every $a\in H^0(C,L)$ consequently acts by a homogeneous linear matrix polynomial $M_a(U,V)\in\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_\kappa(E_A)[U,V]$. These matrix polynomials commute, preserve all polynomial identities among the sections, and satisfy $$M_u=U\,\mathrm{id},\qquad M_v=V\,\mathrm{id},\qquad
     M_z^b=(U^b+V^b)\,\mathrm{id}.$$ Their dependence on $A$ is algebraic on a nonempty $G$-stable open subset of $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^0(C)$. Under transport on this family, $$\label{eq:matrix-transport}
     M_{g_*a}(U,V)
         =(g_{\mathrm{coeff}}M_a)(\chi(g)U,\psi(g)V).$$ Here $g_{\mathrm{coeff}}$ transports the endomorphism coefficients; scalar choices in identifying transported line bundles have no effect.*

4.  *The action of $G$ on $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^1(C)$ is free. For every character $\xi:G\to\mu_b$, there is a continuous map $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^1(C)\to S^1$ equivariant for the given $G$-action and multiplication by $\xi$ on $S^1$.
There are curves, a cover, and a linearized line bundle satisfying parts (i) and (ii) of Proposition 13.
For the curve and line bundle of Lemma 14, part (iii) of Proposition 13 holds.
If a finite group $G$ acts freely on a smooth connected projective complex curve $C$, then its induced action on $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^1(C)$ is free.

Let $q:C\to T$ be a connected étale $G$-cover of smooth connected projective complex curves. For every character $\xi:G\to\mu_b$, there is a continuous map $$f_\xi:\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^1(C)\longrightarrow S^1,\qquad
 f_\xi(g_*A)=\xi(g)f_\xi(A).$$

Let $k$ be a finitely generated extension of the original field $\mathbb C$, and let $\Delta_0$ be a central division algebra over $k$ of degree $e_0$. Fix an integer $b\geq2$, a $k$-vector space $U$ of dimension at least three, and a subspace $$W\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^b(U^\vee),\qquad s=\dim_k W,$$ such that every nonzero member of $W_{\bar k}$ has an irreducible factor of multiplicity one. Choose integers $h,M$ in this order, with $$\label{eq:division-parameters} h\geq \max\bigl(\{2\}\cup \{\,v_p(e_0)s(p^{v_p(b)}-1):p\mid e_0\,\}\bigr), \qquad M\geq2h+4s+10.$$ Here $v_p$ is the $p$-adic valuation, and the prime-indexed set is empty if $e_0=1$. Define $$Y=\left\{(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_M)\in U^{\oplus M}: \sum_{m=1}^M w(\ell_m)=0\quad(w\in W)\right\}, \qquad X=\mathbb P(Y).$$* *Take the curve $C$, group $G$, and linearized line bundle $L$ of Proposition 13 for this $b$. Write $e=|G|=b^b$ and $g_T=b-1$, and put $$B=\prod_{m=2}^M\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^0(C),\qquad H=G^{M-1},\qquad e_1=|H|.$$ All products and curves here are over $k$, and $H$ acts on the corresponding Picard factors by transport from the curve. Choose arbitrary characters $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_M:H\to\mu_b$, and let $H$ act on the points of the $m$-th block of $Y$ by $\rho_m$. Let $R$ be an affine space with a faithful linear $H$-action. Set $$K=k(B\times X\times R),\qquad F=K^H.$$ For the generic tuple of degree-zero line bundles $A_m$, let $$E=\bigotimes_{m=2}^M H^0(C_K,A_m\otimes L^{g_T}).$$ Transport induces a semilinear $H$-action on $\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_K(E)$. Its fixed algebra $\Delta_1=\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_K(E)^H$ is central simple of degree $e_1$ over $F$, and $$\label{eq:division-algebra} \Delta=(\Delta_0\otimes_k F)\otimes_F\Delta_1$$ is a central division algebra of degree $e_0e_1$. Its scalar extension to $K$ identifies with $\Delta_0\otimes_k\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_K(E)$; in the corresponding descent action, $H$ fixes $\Delta_0$ pointwise.
The generic module $\mathcal F_\eta$ extends to a coherent $\Delta_0$-module $\mathcal F$ on $T$ with compatible isomorphisms $J_g\otimes g_*\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal F$.

The sheaf $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal D$ on $Z\times X\times R$ has a genuine $H$-equivariant structure commuting with $\Delta_0$. Its derived restriction to $R=0$ defines an equivariant coherent class $\beta$ on $Z\times X$. Nonequivariantly this class is the tensor product of $\mathcal D$ with a class pulled back from $B\times X$.

For any class $\gamma\in K^0(B)$, $$\int_Z\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}(\operatorname{pr}_B^*\gamma\otimes\mathcal D)\mathop{\mathrm{td}}(Z)
   =\pm\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}\gamma,$$ where the sign is independent of $\gamma$.

Let $Q$ be a projective scheme over a field, and let $\delta:T'\to Q$ be a torsor under a constant finite group of order $a$. For every coherent-sheaf class $\alpha$ on $Q$, $$\chi(T',\delta^*\alpha)=a\,\chi(Q,\alpha).$$

There is an $H'$-equivariant map $$\Phi:\mathbb T\times\mathbb P^h(\mathbb C)\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm{sm}},$$ where $H'$ acts by translation on $\mathbb T$ and trivially on $\mathbb P^h(\mathbb C)$. It has an $H'\times S^1$-equivariant lift $$\widetilde\Phi:\mathbb T\times S^{2h+1}\longrightarrow Y_1.$$ If $t_0\in\mathbb T$ is fixed and $\Phi_0(z)=\Phi(t_0,z)$, then $\Phi$ is homotopic, as an ordinary map, to $\Phi_0$ composed with projection onto $\mathbb P^h(\mathbb C)$, and $$\Phi_0^*\mathcal O_X(-1)\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^h}(-1).$$ There is also an $H$-equivariant map $\vartheta:P\longrightarrow\mathbb T$, for the action through $\rho$.

In the setting of Theorem 18, let $r$ be the reduced rank of any finite right $\Delta$-module. There is a smooth $h$-dimensional linear section $D_0\subset X_{\mathrm{sm}}$, a complete intersection of $s$ hypersurfaces of degree $b$ in $\mathbb P^{h+s}(\mathbb C)$, and integers $q_0,\ldots,q_h\in e_1\mathbb Z$ such that $q_0=\pm r$ and $$\label{eq:index-section-divisibility} \sum_{j=0}^h q_j\, \chi\!\left(D_0, (1-[\mathcal O_{D_0}(-1)])^j\otimes\mathcal O_{D_0}(l)\right) \in e_0e_1\mathbb Z \qquad(l\in\mathbb Z).$$

Let $p$ be a prime, let $v\ge1$, and let $A,Q\in\mathbb Z[u]$. Suppose the reduction of $A$ modulo $p$ has exact order $\nu\ge0$ at $u=0$. If $h\ge v\nu$ and $$A(u)Q(u)=0\pmod{(p^v,u^{h+1})},$$ then $p^v\mid Q(0)$.

Let $b\ge2$, let $k$ contain a primitive $b$-th root of unity $\zeta$, and let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra with elements $u,v$. Introduce symbols $T_\alpha$, indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{b}$ with $|\alpha|=b$, and put $$D_j=T_{b e_j}\quad(0\le j[eq:veronese-exchanges]–[eq:veronese-linear] have degrees two and one.

Fix $1\le i\le n$. Suppose that a field $k$, a central division algebra $\Delta_0$ over $k$, a formal space $U$, and a low-relation ideal $Q\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}_k U$ satisfy the induction conditions of Section 3, with the triangular identities already constructed for the rows $d>i$. Then there are a finitely generated extension $F/k$, a central division algebra $\Delta$ over $F$, and an enlarged formal space and low-relation ideal over $F$ satisfying the same conditions with the rows $d\ge i$ constructed. In particular, the enlarged formal space contains a form $t_i$ for which $$t_i^{a_i} =c_i f_i+\sum_{li}C_{id}t_d \pmod{Q_{\mathrm{new}}}, \qquad c_i\in F^\times. \label{eq:new-triangular-row}$$ All the enlarged formal forms evaluate to mutually commuting linear forms in $\Delta[x]$, and the new relation ideal is generated by linear forms and quadrics.

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $S_F=F[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be standard graded, and put $\mathfrak m=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. Let $$1\le c\le n,\qquad 2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c, \qquad P_F=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c}).$$ Suppose that a homogeneous ideal $I\subseteq S_F$ contains a homogeneous regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ with $\deg f_k=a_k$. Let $J$ be the lex-plus-powers ideal prescribed by Corollary 3 for $P_F$, the order $x_1>\cdots>x_n$, and the Hilbert function of $S_F/I$. For this single ideal, $$\dim_F H^i_{\mathfrak m}(S_F/I)_j \le \dim_F H^i_{\mathfrak m}(S_F/J)_j \qquad(i\ge0,\ j\in\mathbb Z).$$

Let $F$ have characteristic zero, let $r\ge1$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb P^r_F$ be a zero-dimensional scheme-theoretic complete intersection of $r$ quadrics, of degree $2^r$. For an integer $1\le k\le r$ and a degree-$k$ hypersurface $X\subseteq\mathbb P^r_F$, $$\Omega\not\subseteq X
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \deg(\Omega\cap X)\le 2^r-2^{r-k}.$$ Equivalently, if $X$ contains a closed subscheme of $\Omega$ of degree strictly greater than $2^r-2^{r-k}$, then it contains $\Omega$ scheme-theoretically. Degrees here mean scheme lengths over $F$; no reducedness assumption is needed.
